title: A hand on the handle
note: The door does not move in this one. That is the point of the rung: the sound and sight of the handle being touched, with nothing opening.
scene: Interior entry hall, side view, camera at standing eye level. This is the same room, the same camera position and the same distance from the viewer as the other rungs of this ladder: Lucy's rectangular cool-grey dog bed on the left, the closed charcoal front door on the right, and a clear span of taupe-grey floor between them, with the whole walk from bed to door visible in frame. Lucy lies on the bed in a settled down — elbows and hips on the bed, head up and level, watching calmly. Her size in frame, the bed's position and the camera never change between these pictures. No leash. Only one thing changes from the previous rung: the handler now stands at the closed front door with one hand resting on its handle. She stands still and relaxed, in profile to the viewer, looking at the door rather than at Lucy. The door has not moved: it is fully shut in its frame, no gap, no daylight, no shadow of an opening. Lucy holds her down on the bed across the room.
mustBeTrue: the door is completely shut with no gap and no daylight showing, the handler's hand rests on the handle without pulling it, and Lucy holds her down on the bed.
